revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Overtime Hours Limit
revealWordProblem.text: Detective Chen's team can use at most 40 hours of overtime this week to close the case. So far the team has logged 26 hours. Write an inequality for the additional overtime hours t the team can still use, solve it, and graph the solution set on a number line.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The inequality is 26 + t ≤ 40. Subtracting 26 from both sides: t ≤ 40 − 26 = 14. Since ≤ includes the boundary, graph a closed circle at 14 and shade left (toward smaller values), meaning the team can use 14 or fewer additional overtime hours this week.

questions.stem: A museum has some paintings. After adding 12, they have 45. Which equation models this?
questions.explanation: 'Adding 12' to the original number gives 45: p + 12 = 45. Solve: p = 33.
choiceFeedback: Subtracting says the museum LOST paintings, but 12 were ADDED to what they had. Choose the operation that matches 'after adding 12.'
12p means 12 groups of p, which is multiplication. Re-read what actually happened to the paintings the museum already had.
Dividing would split the paintings into 12 equal groups. The museum did something different with the 12.
hints: The museum STARTS with an unknown number of paintings p, then 12 more are ADDED to reach 45.
'Adding 12' means the model joins p and 12 with a plus sign, and the total 45 goes after the equals sign.
Write the story in order: p, plus 12, equals 45. Which choice matches without switching the operation?
questions.stemEs: Un museo tiene algunas pinturas. Después de agregar 12, tiene 45. ¿Qué ecuación representa esta situación?
questions.explanationEs: «Agregar 12» al número original da 45: p + 12 = 45. Resuelve: p = 33.
hintsEs: El museo EMPIEZA con un número desconocido de cuadros p y luego se AGREGAN 12 más para llegar a 45.
'Agregar 12' significa que el modelo une p y 12 con un signo más, y el total 45 va después del signo igual.
Escribe la historia en orden: p, más 12, es igual a 45. ¿Qué opción coincide sin cambiar la operación?

questions.stem: A detective needs more than 8 hours to finish the investigation. She has already worked 3 hours. Which inequality represents the additional hours h she needs?
questions.explanation: 3 hours plus additional hours h must be more than 8: 3 + h > 8. Solve: h > 5.
choiceFeedback: The equals sign pins her total to EXACTLY 8 hours, but she needs more than 8. Keep the total 3 + h and swap in the comparison the story demands.
This compares the extra hours to 3, but 3 is the time already worked, not the goal. It is the total of both amounts that has to pass 8.
The 8 and the 3 have swapped jobs here. 8 is the total she must go past, and 3 is what she has already finished.
hints: There are two time pieces: the 3 hours already worked and the extra hours h. Together they must pass 8 hours.
'More than 8' means the TOTAL of 3 + h sits on the big side of a strict inequality — not an equals sign.
Combine first: 3 + h. Then compare that total to 8 using the strict 'more than' symbol. Which choice is built that way?
questions.stemEs: Una detective necesita más de 8 horas para terminar la investigación. Ya trabajó 3 horas. ¿Qué desigualdad representa las horas adicionales h que necesita?
questions.explanationEs: 3 horas más las horas adicionales h deben ser más de 8: 3 + h > 8. Resuelve: h > 5.
hintsEs: Hay dos partes de tiempo: las 3 horas ya trabajadas y las horas extra h. Juntas deben pasar de 8 horas.
'Más de 8' significa que el TOTAL de 3 + h queda del lado grande de una desigualdad estricta, no de un signo igual.
Combina primero: 3 + h. Luego compara ese total con 8 usando el símbolo estricto de 'más de'. ¿Qué opción está armada así?

questions.stem: Which model is correct for: 'A number divided by 6 equals 7'?
questions.explanation: Divided by 6 is n / 6. Equals 7 means = 7. So n / 6 = 7.
choiceFeedback: That shows subtracting 6. The words say divided by 6.
hints: Spot the operation phrase: 'divided by 6'. That phrase gives you the symbol between n and 6.
Keep the sentence order — the number n comes first, then the division by 6, then 'equals 7'.
Write n / 6 on the left and 7 on the right. Which choice shows division rather than multiplying or adding 6?
questions.stemEs: ¿Qué modelo es correcto para: 'Un número dividido entre 6 es igual a 7'?
questions.explanationEs: Dividido entre 6 es n / 6. Es igual a 7 significa = 7. Entonces n / 6 = 7.
hintsEs: Identifica la frase de operación: 'dividido entre 6'. Esa frase te da el símbolo entre n y 6.
Conserva el orden de la oración: el número n va primero, luego la división entre 6 y luego 'es igual a 7'.
Escribe n / 6 a la izquierda y 7 a la derecha. ¿Qué opción muestra división en vez de multiplicar o sumar 6?

reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Equations and Inequalities Problem Solving is matching the wrong model to a key phrase. For 'the getaway car held no more than 6 bags,' students often write the equation b = 6 instead of the inequality b ≤ 6, because they see one number and assume it must be exact. The same mistake happens in reverse: for 'the reward split equally among 5 people gave each $40,' students sometimes write the inequality 5p ≥ 40 instead of the equation 5p = 40, because 'split equally' sounds like it could mean a range. Before you submit, ask: does this phrase give one exact value (equation, =) or a limit/range (inequality, <, >, ≤, ≥)?

level1.stem: A bus can carry at most 48 passengers. There are already 31 on board. Which inequality shows how many more can board?
level1.explanation: 'At most 48' means the total must be ≤ 48. So 31 + p ≤ 48. Solve: p ≤ 17.
choiceFeedback: Your total 31 + p is built right — the symbol is the problem. 'At most' is a ceiling: can the bus legally leave exactly full? Pick the symbol that allows it.
An equals sign forces the bus to end up exactly full. Think about whether “at most” also allows a total below the limit.
Subtracting takes away the 31 riders who are already aboard. They belong with the new riders, not apart from them.
hints: The bus already has 31 riders, and p more may board — but the TOTAL cannot pass 48.
'At most 48' allows exactly 48 but nothing above it, so you need the symbol with the 'or equal' bar, not > or =.
Add the parts first: 31 + p. Then cap that sum at 48 with the 'at most' symbol. Which choice matches?
level1.stemEs: Un autobús puede llevar como máximo 48 pasajeros. Ya hay 31 a bordo. ¿Qué desigualdad muestra cuántos más pueden subir?
level1.explanationEs: «Como máximo 48» significa que el total debe ser ≤ 48. Entonces 31 + p ≤ 48. Resuelve: p ≤ 17.
hintsEs: El autobús ya lleva 31 pasajeros y pueden subir p más, pero el TOTAL no puede pasar de 48.
'A lo sumo 48' permite exactamente 48 pero nada por encima, así que necesitas el símbolo con la barra de 'o igual', no > ni =.
Suma primero las partes: 31 + p. Luego limita esa suma a 48 con el símbolo de 'a lo sumo'. ¿Qué opción coincide?

level2.stem: A student solved 4n = 52 and got n = 13. Is the answer reasonable if n represents the number of notebooks in a box?
choices: Yes — 13 notebooks per box is reasonable
Yes — but only if n is a fraction
level2.explanation: 4 × 13 = 52 ✓. 13 notebooks per box is a reasonable whole number answer.
choiceFeedback: Too many by what measure? A box holding 13 notebooks is ordinary. Reasonableness asks whether the number fits the situation, not whether it feels big.
48 comes from subtracting 4 from 52, but 4n means 4 times n. Multiplication is undone with division.
Notebooks are counted in whole numbers, and substituting the solution back into 4n = 52 works out exactly. No fraction is needed here.
hints: 'Reasonable' asks two things: does the math check out, AND does the number make sense for notebooks in a box?
Check the math first: multiply 4 by 13 and see if it rebuilds 52. Then judge whether that count fits a real box of notebooks.
Compute 4 × 13. Does it equal 52? Then ask: could a box realistically hold that many notebooks? Match your reasoning to one choice.

level2.explanationEs: 4 × 13 = 52 ✓. 13 cuadernos por caja es una respuesta razonable con un número entero.
choicesEs: Sí — 13 cuadernos por caja es razonable

hintsEs: 'Razonable' pregunta dos cosas: ¿cuadran las cuentas Y tiene sentido ese número de cuadernos en una caja?
Revisa primero las cuentas: multiplica 4 por 13 y ve si reconstruye 52. Luego juzga si esa cantidad cabe en una caja real de cuadernos.
Calcula 4 × 13. ¿Da 52? Luego pregunta: ¿podría una caja tener realmente esa cantidad de cuadernos? Une tu razonamiento con una opción.

level3.stem: A school van can carry at most 14 passengers. There are already 9 passengers on board. Let p be the number of additional passengers who can get on. Which inequality models this situation?
choiceFeedback: This demands at least 14, which would let the van overfill. 'At most' caps the total.
This forbids a full van of exactly 14. 'At most 14' allows 14.
This subtracts the riders already aboard. They add to the total, so 9 plus p.
level3.explanation: The 9 passengers already on board plus the p additional passengers make up the total. The phrase 'at most 14' means that total may reach 14 but cannot pass it, so the model is 9 + p ≤ 14.

level3.prompt: Create two word problems about the same situation: one that requires an equation and one that requires an inequality. Solve both and explain why the models are different.
level3.sentenceFrame: Equation problem: ___. Model: ___. Solution: ___. Inequality problem: ___. Model: ___. Solution: ___. The models are different because ___.
level3.hint: Use a strategy or example from the lesson to help you explain your answer.
hints: Use the same situation twice: one question asks for an EXACT amount, the other sets a limit or a minimum.
Choose clue words on purpose: 'exactly' or 'in total' for your equation; 'at least', 'at most', or 'more than' for your inequality.
Pick a scene, like saving money. Write 'I saved exactly $__' for the equation, then 'I need at least $__' for the inequality. Solve both and compare.
level3.explanation: The two models differ because the two questions ask for different things. An equation fits when the situation names one exact amount, like 'I saved exactly $45', so it has a single solution. An inequality fits when the situation sets a minimum or a ceiling, like 'I need at least $45', so a whole range of values works. Same story, different clue words, different symbol.
level3.explanationEs: Los dos modelos son distintos porque las dos preguntas piden cosas distintas. Una ecuación sirve cuando la situación nombra una cantidad exacta, como 'ahorré exactamente $45', así que tiene una sola solución. Una desigualdad sirve cuando la situación pone un mínimo o un tope, como 'necesito al menos $45', así que funciona todo un rango de valores. La misma historia, distintas palabras clave, distinto símbolo.
level3.promptEs: Crea dos problemas sobre la misma situación: uno que requiera una ecuación y otro que requiera una desigualdad. Resuelve los dos y explica por qué los modelos son diferentes.
hintsEs: Usa la misma situación dos veces: una pregunta pide una cantidad EXACTA y la otra fija un límite o un mínimo.
Escoge las palabras clave a propósito: 'exactamente' o 'en total' para tu ecuación; 'al menos', 'a lo sumo' o 'más de' para tu desigualdad.
Escoge una escena, como ahorrar dinero. Escribe 'Ahorré exactamente $__' para la ecuación y luego 'Necesito al menos $__' para la desigualdad. Resuelve ambas y compara.
